$comment: The jp theme's road cross-sections: Japanese road markings drawn on Jakarta's roads.
Read by scripts/build-jp-roads.mjs (which bakes the road surfaces and markings into the tileset) and src/jp-roads.ts (which styles them), so the two cannot disagree.
Sources: 道路標識、区画線及び道路標示に関する命令 (S35総理府・建設省令3, as in force 2026-09-01) 別表第三〜第六;
MLIT circular 区画線の設置様式について (S49.12.26 都街発67・道企発99), whose standard values are what is actually painted;
道路構造令 第5条 (lane widths) and 第8条 (shoulders). All lengths in metres.
Every cross-section is symmetric about its centre, so a road reads the same whichever way it was drawn.
Each `lines` entry is drawn at +offset and -offset (once when offset is 0). `dash` is [painted, gap]; omitted means solid.

The baked tileset is shared by every theme: jp draws its markings, light and dark only the surfaces and kerbs. Paint features carry k: kerb (the asphalt outline), edge (edge lines) or mark (everything else).

pavement: mapped sidewalks (OSM footway=sidewalk) paved as a widthM strip joined to the nearest kerb within reachM, surface paving `sidewalk`; pedestrian streets (kind_detail pedestrian) a streetWidthM strip. Light and dark draw it as Apple Maps' block edges; jp leaves it out.

medians: planted strips between carriageways, inferred (OSM barely maps them): a named road's carriageways and the busways along it, closed over gaps up to maxWidthM, minus every road surface, kept in pieces at least minLengthM long; surface paving `median`, light and dark only. Only on the stretches listed: a road (name contains `name`) inside `box` ([W, S, E, N], lon/lat), where its medians are known to be green.
highwayKinds: roads paved `highway` on top of the asphalt, so light and dark keep toll roads tinted up close; jp draws them as asphalt.
tileset: the baked roads (scripts/build-jp-roads.mjs), versioned by name: bump it whenever it is rebuilt with different geometry or markings, since tiles are cached for a day.
boldStripeFactor: stripes are drawn this much wider at minzoom, easing to true width at trueFromZoom, so a 0.15 m line is visible at z17.
kerbRadiusM: inside corners where roads meet are rounded to this radius, like a kerb return (5 m is a common urban radius), and only near junctions, so medians between one-way pairs stay open.
smoothing: centrelines are drawn as a curve through the OSM vertices (centripetal Catmull-Rom), resampled every stepM, except across turns sharper than maxTurnDeg, which stay corners.

Rows with `link: true` match only link roads (ramps); every other row excludes them. Rows with `named: true` match only roads that have a name. Rows with no `lines` are surface only: they make the road network one continuous plane without being marked.

edge: true marks a 車道外側線. Except on motorways, edge lines are not offset per road: they are the outline of the merged road surface inset by the shoulder, so they follow every kerb return round a corner and never cross a junction mouth, as real edge lines do.

hiddenAccess (per row): roads of that row with these OSM access values are not drawn. Only service roads use it: a building's internal roads are private service roads, while gated neighbourhood streets (Kebayoran's portal streets, Jalan Lamandau) are private too but residential, named, and real streets. Never `no`: TransJakarta busways and some bus-only ramps are tagged access=no.
edgesAlongRoad: true keeps a row's edge lines as per-road offsets (motorways: their wider shoulder differs from the 0.5 m every other row shares, and they meet nothing at grade).

Access roads: surface only, so the street network reads as one plane. Named ones only: the tiles drop OSM's service=* subtype, so a mall's lobby loops and parking aisles (Grand Indonesia) look exactly like a public service lane, except that they have no name.
Gang and living streets: surface only.

rows.note: TransJakarta busway lanes as a Japanese bus-only lane: coloured paving (a common Japanese treatment, colour not set by the ordinance) inside yellow no-lane-change lines. The painted バス専用 text (109の6) is not drawn: a line pattern cannot place it, and PT Sans has no kana.
